component.name: Airloom
component.summary: See the air around you, sensor by sensor

description.p: Airloom is a focused air-quality map for Fedora. It presents nearby public PurpleAir readings, recent trends, favorites, and local AQI threshold alerts in a GNOME-friendly desktop interface.
Airloom includes a clearly labeled demo mode and accepts a personal PurpleAir read key for live data.
Place-search navigation now shows the sensors at the destination instead of leaving the map empty, and the area AQI chip is labeled with the area currently in view rather than always showing home.

Location detection now works on first launch: the permission request waits for the app window to gain focus so GNOME's location dialog can appear, a fix arriving after the detection timeout is still applied, and a failed first-run detection is reported honestly instead of showing the default area as a known location.
Small towns are now labeled by name rather than by their county.
Location detection now distinguishes precise fixes from coarse IP-level guesses and never overwrites a known location with the wrong city.
Automatic location detection, place search, and redesigned map-first interface with persistent tile rendering and independent alert timers.
Hardening release: resilient refreshes, safer external-link handling, private config storage, the full piecewise EPA smoke correction, and automatic background refresh for alerts.
